### 2026-10-05 — Today I started planning my custom Stream Deck project. My goal is to make a compact desktop controller with six programmable buttons, one volume knob, and a screen that shows the function assigned to

**2.5h**

Today I started planning my custom Stream Deck project. My goal is to make a compact desktop controller with six programmable buttons, one volume knob, and a screen that shows the function assigned to each button.

I first decided on the main features I wanted. I chose six buttons because it gives me enough controls without making the device too large. I also decided to include a rotary encoder for volume control. Turning the knob will increase or decrease the volume, and I will use the built-in push button for mute or changing modes.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/8S48ZFAF3eXNPqG1Hk6qDsr1e0r98gyj/85d8ae61c30ca09cae85923de63b2164fc14aa93808eefe429ae448aa8f0b539.png)

I spent time thinking about the screen layout. Instead of using a very small OLED screen, I decided that a small color TFT display would be better because it can show six button labels clearly. The screen will display a layout that matches the physical buttons so the user can easily see what each button does.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/8S48ZFAF3eXNPqG1Hk6qDsr1e0r98gyj/eb458aec9cb4a63e8e850da3e0cfaef57e3e0f312456d19a9caaa6e8538a5bc6.png)

I also planned the physical arrangement of the controls. The screen will be near the top of the device, with the six buttons arranged in two rows of three underneath it. The volume knob will be placed on the right side.

For the electronics, I am planning to use an RP2040 microcontroller because it can work as a USB keyboard and media controller. The six buttons will connect to GPIO pins, the display will use SPI, and the rotary encoder will use separate GPIO pins.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/8S48ZFAF3eXNPqG1Hk6qDsr1e0r98gyj/e54219955d96ee4190c4ccb857315778f94959736a445b18873e95ad4df095f4.png)

Decisions Made

- 6 programmable mechanical buttons
- 1 rotary encoder for volume (twist knob)
- Push-button function on the volume knob (mute/unmute)
- Color TFT display
- RP2040-based microcontroller (raspberry pi pico)
- 2×3 button layout
- Custom PCB
- Screen labels that match each button

### 2026-10-06 — Today I spent about 2.1 hours working on the design for my custom Stream Deck. I sketched out the overall layout of the device and decided where the main components will be placed.

**2.1h**

Today I spent about 2.1 hours working on the design for my custom Stream Deck. I sketched out the overall layout of the device and decided where the main components will be placed.
I decided to use mechanical buttons for the main controls because they should feel better to press and make the Stream Deck feel more like a real keyboard or macropad.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/8S48ZFAF3eXNPqG1Hk6qDsr1e0r98gyj/4700f5b62cf407bf2e7d0dfb09ba4c3e944d9dabf16e9b52b84badb1aca72fe9.png)
I also decided to add 10 RGB 5 mm LEDs. These will be placed in a row between the buttons. My plan is to use them for lighting effects and possibly to show different modes, actions, or statuses depending on what the Stream Deck is doing.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/8S48ZFAF3eXNPqG1Hk6qDsr1e0r98gyj/ba5455deb0a4f0292a91a425ba211aebc2e56b7f574941dd978a5dad01cc8e66.png)
I am also going to add a small OLED display dedicated to volume. The OLED will show a volume indication bar, so when I turn the volume knob I can visually see the current volume level.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/8S48ZFAF3eXNPqG1Hk6qDsr1e0r98gyj/7541deeefba036b86754cc026f41cf6b3af8de13d228786bc9cd0251480568d4.png)
The design currently includes:
- Mechanical push buttons
- 10 × 5 mm RGB LEDs
- RGB LED row between the buttons
- OLED display for the volume bar
- Rotary knob for volume control
- Main screen for button functions
During this session, I mainly focused on the physical layout and how the controls should be organized. I also drew a rough sketch to help plan the positions and spacing of the buttons, LEDs, screens, and volume knob.
